doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: The Basie band, its leaders, and the Freddie Green remark
summary: Basie was the favorite band; successors Foster, Mitchell, Freddie Green; an embarrassing remark to Green.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Why did you have such a close association with the Basie Band?

It was always my favorite band. It was the Sauter-Finegan favorite band. We had a night off in Wichita and we all conned Joe Gray, our bus driver, to take us to hear Count Basie. The whole Sauter-Finegan band went to hear Count Basie. No, that was our favorite band. That was our idea of a jazz band.
Do you like what’s happened with the band since the Count passed on?

They’ve kept the tradition. They’ve played a few new things here and there, but they play a lot of the old things. Frank Foster had the band for a time, Grover Mitchell has the band now I think. Freddie Green, the guitar player, had the band for a while.
He doesn’t seem like the leader type, but you never know—
No. Freddie’s not the leader type, but he was. The guys in the band respected him.

Thad Jones was the leader of the band. I hate to forget names, but just people I associate with. Something humorous to me personally was when Freddie Green had the band and at intermission I went up to Freddie and I says, “Freddie, I want you to meet Mike Scott.” I says, “I’ve got three of them in the band” meaning three brothers. They are three black cats I had in the band. And Freddie thought I meant I had three black cats in the band, and that I was trying to be—

Trying to be hip. And I got a look from him that I don’t believe. I saw Clark Terry two weeks later and I says, “How well do you know Freddie Green?” He says, “Very well.” I says, “Will you go to Freddie and explain to him who the hell I am and what I meant by that remark?” I told him what I had said and Freddie’s reaction. I said, “I was never so embarrassed in my life.” Anyway—
I’ll bet Clark got a kick out of it.
